title: Leonard Feather misquoting him over Gene Krupa
summary: Roy complains he was misquoted over his remarks about Gene hiring him and white bands.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x:
Oh yeah. Also the other Smith, Russell Smith, used to play "Time On My Hands" and ...[?]... They played pretty things. But so could the White bands play pretty things. And that just wasn't my thing, you know.

You got to watch saying that, now, because we'll get another Leonard Feather deal going on here! Boy, that cat really hung me on the wall with that. Boy, that was really wrong, man. Talk about misquoting people. At any rate, it was just like that fight, that Gerry Cooney fight, you know. All of a sudden, I should be very thankful that Gene... Gene didn't hire me because I was Black. He hired me because I could play. Right? And I could play before he hired me! But still then, everybody said, "Oh, you should be ashamed of yourself, because Gene gave you this break and..." Well, bullshit, man! Because it pulled his band up, too, with me being there. But then there were the other people, like Lena Horne said, "You had too much French rubbed off on
you." And all I said, when you asked me...
